plain.headline: Use What God Gives
plain.intro: Near the end of the Church year, the readings ask what we are doing with the gifts God has placed in our hands while we wait for Christ to return. Proverbs praises a woman whose hard work and open hands make her worth more than jewels, and Paul tells us to stay awake as children of the light. In the Gospel, Jesus tells of three servants trusted with their master's money: two put it to work, and one buries it out of fear.
plain.listen: what each servant does with what he was given

Reading 1.box: The Book of Proverbs closes with a poem praising a capable wife who works hard, earns her husband's complete trust, and opens her hands to the poor. What makes her worthy of praise is not charm or beauty but her reverence for the Lord. In Hebrew the poem is an alphabet poem, each line beginning with the next letter.

chunks.text: Who can find a capable wife? She is worth far more than jewels. Her husband trusts her with all his heart, and he will never be in need. She does him good and never harm, every day of her life.

She gathers wool and flax and works gladly with her hands. She sets her hands to the spinning and holds the spindle in her fingers. She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to those in need.
Charm can fool you, and beauty fades, but a woman who honors the Lord deserves praise. Give her a share of what her hands have made, and let her works speak her praise at the city gates.

Responsorial Psalm.box: This psalm blesses the person who honors God and walks in his ways. It pictures a happy home, where work bears fruit and the children gather around the table like young olive trees.

Reading 2.box: The Christians in Thessalonica wanted to know when the Lord would return. Paul says no one knows the time, since that day will come like a thief in the night. But believers live in the light, so they should stay awake and clear-headed.

chunks.text: Brothers and sisters, you do not need anyone to write to you about times and dates. You know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. Just when people are saying, 'All is peaceful and safe,' sudden ruin will come on them, like labor pains on a woman about to give birth, and they will not escape.

But you, brothers and sisters, are not in the dark, so that day should not catch you by surprise like a thief. You are all children of the light and children of the day. We do not belong to the night or to darkness. So let us not sleep like the others, but stay awake and clear-headed.

Gospel.box: Jesus tells this parable a few days before his death, as part of his teaching about the end of time. A talent was a huge sum of money, about twenty years of wages for a laborer. The master stands for Christ, who will return, and the money for everything God entrusts to us, to be used and not buried.

chunks.text: "It is like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and handed his property over to them. To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, each according to his ability. Then he left on his journey.

Right away the servant who had received five talents went and traded with them, and earned five more. In the same way, the one who had two earned two more. But the one who had received one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master's money.

After a long time the master of those servants came back and settled accounts with them. The one who had received five talents came forward with five more and said, 'Master, you gave me five talents. Look, I have earned five more.' His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant. You were faithful in small things, so I will put you in charge of great things. Come and share your master's joy.'

The one who had two talents also came forward and said, 'Master, you gave me two talents. Look, I have earned two more.' His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant. You were faithful in small things, so I will put you in charge of great things. Come and share your master's joy.'

Then the one who had received one talent came forward and said, 'Master, I knew you were a hard man, harvesting where you did not plant and gathering where you did not scatter seed. So I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you have what is yours.'

His master answered, 'You wicked, lazy servant. So you knew that I harvest where I did not plant and gather where I did not scatter? Then you should have put my money in the bank, and when I came back I would have received it back with interest.

Take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten. For whoever has will be given more, and he will have plenty. But whoever has nothing, even what he has will be taken away. And throw this useless servant out into the darkness outside, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.'"

plain.carry: This week I will name one gift God has given me and put it to use for someone else, instead of burying it out of fear.

kids.headline: Share Your Gifts
kids.intro: Today's readings are about using the gifts God gives us. Jesus tells a story about three servants who were each given money to take care of while their master was away. Two of them used it well, and one was too afraid to do anything with it.
kids.listen: what the third servant does with his money

Reading 1.box: This reading praises a woman who works hard, takes good care of her family, and helps poor people. It says that loving God matters more than being pretty or charming.

chunks.text: A good and faithful wife is worth more than the most precious jewels. Her husband trusts her completely. She is good to him every day of her life. She works hard and happily, making cloth with her hands.

She spins thread to make clothes. She reaches out to help poor people and anyone in need. Being charming or pretty does not last, but a woman who loves and honors God deserves praise. Let everyone see the good work of her hands and praise her for it.

Responsorial Psalm.box: This song says that people who love God and follow his ways will be happy. It pictures a family gathered around the dinner table, blessed by God.

Reading 2.box: Saint Paul says no one knows when Jesus will come again. It will be a surprise, like a robber coming at night. But people who love Jesus live in his light, so they can stay awake and ready.

chunks.text: Paul says, "You already know that the day the Lord comes will be a surprise, like a robber who comes in the night. Some people will say, 'Everything is fine and safe,' and then trouble will come on them all at once, and they will not get away.

But you are not living in the dark, so that day will not catch you by surprise. You are children of the light and children of the day. So let's not be sleepy like the others. Let's stay awake and ready."

Gospel.box: Jesus tells a story about a master who trusted his servants with his money, called talents, while he went on a trip. When he came back, he wanted to see what they had done with it. God gives each of us gifts, and he hopes we will use them well.

chunks.text: Jesus told a story. A man was going on a long trip. He called his servants and gave them his money to take care of. He gave one servant five bags of money, called talents, another servant two bags, and another one bag, depending on how much each could handle. Then he left.
The servant with five bags went right to work and earned five more. The servant with two bags earned two more. But the servant with one bag dug a hole in the ground and hid the money.

After a long time, the master came home. The servant who had five bags brought ten. The master said, 'Well done, good and faithful servant. You took good care of a little, so I will trust you with much more. Come and share my joy.' The servant who had two bags brought four, and the master said the very same thing to him.
Then the servant with one bag came. He said, 'Master, I knew you were tough and demanding. I was afraid, so I hid your money in the ground. Here it is.'

The master said, 'You were lazy and did not do what you should. You could at least have put my money in the bank to earn a little more.' He took the one bag away and gave it to the servant who had ten. He said, 'Whoever uses what he has will be given more, and whoever does nothing will lose even what he has.' Then the lazy servant was sent out into the dark, where there is crying and great sadness.

word.meaning: In Jesus' time, a talent was a very large amount of money. Today we also use the word for a gift or skill God gives us.

kids.draw: Draw yourself using one of your gifts, like singing, helping, or drawing, to make someone else happy.
kids.ask: What is one gift God has given you, and how can you use it this week?

family.opener: Today Jesus tells a story about three servants who were trusted with their master's money, and what each one did while the master was away.
questions: What gifts has God given each person in our family?
Why do you think the third servant was so afraid, and what might have helped him trust his master?
The woman in the first reading reaches out to the poor; how can our family use what we have to help someone in need?
family.try: Have each person name one gift they see in someone else in the family, then plan one way to use your gifts together to help a neighbor, a friend, or your parish.
family.pray: Generous God, thank you for every gift you have given our family, and help us use them bravely to serve you and others.
